title: fix: keep New Session tooltip from blocking sidebar controls
body: Fixes #187088. ## What Problem This Solves Hovering the sidebar rail’s New Session button opens a shortcut hint to its right. When that hint overlaps a neighboring session-group header, its keycap text receives the pointer instead of the header. Moving directly from the plus button to the group can prevent the group’s normal controls from responding. ## User Impact The pointer can reach the adjacent group header and its actions while the informational hint is visible. The hint keeps its content, placement, and accessible description. New Session remains a native link: context menus, middle-click, and modified-click keep their normal behavior, and opening the form does not create a conversation or discard an unsent draft. ## Why This Change Was Made The New Session link owns a read-only tooltip containing a shortcut hint or disabled explanation. It now opts into the shared tooltip’s existing `pointerThrough` capability. The shared default remains unchanged, so rich tooltips containing links continue to accept pointer input. No permission checks, routing rules, styles, timers, or new interaction mechanism are introduced. The existing sidebar interaction scenario now waits for the rail tooltip to actually open and moves directly to the neighboring header. Removing the intermediate composer hover prevents the test from passing by dismissing the hint before it reaches the obstructed control. Group/catalog URLs, native-tab gestures, draft preservation, and no-session-creation assertions remain intact. The contribution adds one production line; the existing test changes by ten added and two removed lines. ## Evidence On base `700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337`, the strengthened compiled Chromium scenario fails at the original header hover: the shortcut’s `span.kbd__text` intercepts pointer events for the 30-second action timeout. The other four sidebar cases pass. The current integrated tree passes changed-file formatting/lint, the selected UI and consumer type graphs, and all five sidebar interaction cases. That file took 31.72 seconds, including its UI build and native browser-tab journey. Existing resident-link/shell controls and all 29 tooltip cases in each of Chromium and WebKit also pass; those results were reused after verifying that their relevant sources and dependencies are unchanged. Independent source review and the separate structured review found no actionable defects. The matched live guest captures below use the same blank conversation, viewport, theme, route, tooltip geometry, and pointer coordinates. On the original base, the hint receives the click and the group stays expanded. On `20cf502d23566e71d6af1c71b9e692eac6ac3db0`, the header receives the click and collapses. Both runs preserve the unsent draft and produce zero session-creation requests. The existing Gateway’s relevant contracts are unchanged; this is local UI behavior proof rather than whole-Gateway qualification. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40795951875) passed all seven mocked UI shards and all three UI unit shards. Its three failing rows were traced to existing mock-export, sessions-send lint, and restart-history defects. The [main-branch run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40796541972) reproduces the same mock and restart failures; the lint error also reproduces on the exact CI parent. The mock correction has landed in #187120; the restart repair is tracked by #187143. These failed statuses remain explicit. On the current target, the direct pointer scenario still fails without this fix, while all five sidebar cases pass with it, including the agent-menu changes already on main. The contribution fits the measured test-code capacity restored by #187162. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Shortcut hint intercepts the header click and the group stays expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0257ba7f-f050-43c4-8fb6-41e6d20754f4) | ![Pointer reaches the group header and collapses it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45eccda0-3cb9-4fed-8622-fc88464116dc) | ### Before and after: real pointer movement and one header click https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfc6fd48-6f68-4bb0-92e0-0970592c551e ### Visual verification - Baseline: 700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337 - Exact head: `20cf502d23566e71d6af1c71b9e692eac6ac3db0` - Scenario: Hover the rail New Session button until its shortcut hint opens, move directly to the adjacent group header, and click once\. Desktop viewport1440×900; matched720×300 crops exclude unrelated content\. - Runtime/build: Current\-source Control UI on an existing isolated guest Gateway; matched viewport, route, fixture, theme and pointer coordinates\. Backend09a58215 unchanged\. - Header rectangle: x62,y48,width237,height24 on both revisions - Tooltip rectangle: x48\.5,y53\.125,width153\.015625,height25\.75 on both revisions - Header response: Before: stays expanded; after: collapses - Protected state: Unsent draft preserved;0session\-creation requests on both runs - Actual live guest connection; no model turn - Pointer movement and input cue shown - Native\-link regression: red before, green after; all original assertions retained - Shared interactive rich\-tooltip browser control passes - Matched crops omit unrelated UI without hiding the measured interaction
